newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: IAEA to resume talks with North Korea in January.
newsitem.headline: IAEA to resume talks with North Korea in January.

text.p: The International Atomic Energy Agency said on Tuesday it planned to resume nuclear talks with North Korea in January after both sides failed to reach an agreement in the last round in September.
The talks relate to the agency's monitoring of North Korea's freeze on its nuclear programme, agreed in October 1994 as part of a deal with the United States.

"The next round of technical discussions with North Korea is scheduled to take place in January 1997," IAEA Director General Hans Blix told the Vienna-based organisation's Board of Governors at the start of a two-day closed-door meeting.
He reiterated that no progress had been made in the previous meeting on "important issues which include the preservation of information".
Pyongyang's communist government agreed in a pact with Washington in 1994 to halt its nuclear plant-building programme in exchange for the provision of light-water models.
Light-water reactors produce less of the plutonium the West feared North Korea was using to develop a nuclear bomb.

On the subject of trafficking in nuclear material, Blix said a system was now in place for reporting incidents of trafficking but that the data was still insufficient to detect trends in frequency or type of material involved.
"We cannot therefore read very much into the apparent reduction in the frequency of incidents in the last months," he said.
He stressed the potential for theft of nuclear materials due to poor security and said the IAEA was seeking closer cooperation with international bodies to prevent this.
He said the IAEA was also dealing with other areas of concern including strengthening nuclear safeguards, monitoring of Iraqi weapons programmes, and waste disposal.
